summary: A single-user home library for tracking personal books and who has borrowed them. Add books with title, author, and kind (Novel/Cookbook/Reference/Other), view the full collection, lend a book out by noting a borrower's name, mark it returned, edit or delete mistaken entries, filter to just the books currently out, and see a live count of how many are lent out. All data persists in the browser via localStorage so it survives a page refresh.
implemented_features: Add a book (title, author, kind/category) with validation and empty/invalid input handling
List every book in one collection view
Lend a book out by recording a borrower's name (clears on return)
Return a lent book, clearing the borrower
Edit an existing book to fix mistakes
Filter the collection to only books currently lent out
Derived count of how many books are lent out right now
Data persists across a browser refresh via localStorage
Malformed persisted data is sanitized/dropped so the app keeps working
Domain logic, persistence, and UI kept behind separate boundaries
assumptions: The idea mentions 'roughly what kind of book it is' with examples novel/cookbook/reference; I implemented a fixed category list (Novel, Cookbook, Reference, Other) as a select rather than free text, to keep the list consistent and filterable while still covering the named kinds and an Other fallback.

Single-user, own computer: no login or backend is needed. Data is stored locally in the browser via localStorage; if storage is unavailable or corrupt the app degrades gracefully to an in-memory session.
Borrower is captured as a free-text name (no contact info) since the idea only asks to 'note down their name'; lending requires a non-empty name, and returning clears it.
The idea does not request search/sort, due dates, or a history of past loans, so those were omitted to avoid inventing capabilities the idea does not justify.
Deletion is guarded by a confirm dialog to prevent accidental data loss, consistent with the 'take it off the list' requirement being recoverable on mistake.

tests_run.journey: Add a book with title, author, and category, then see it appear in the collection
Adding a book with empty fields is rejected and shows validation errors
Lend a book by entering a borrower name; it shows as out with someone and the lent-out count increments; returning it clears the borrower and decrements the count
Filter the collection to show only books currently lent out, hiding at-home books
Edit an existing book to fix a mistaken title and see the corrected entry
Delete a book after confirming and confirm it is removed from the collection
Books persist across a page refresh (new app instance loads previously saved data)
Domain logic: create, lend (with trimming and blank-name rejection), return, edit, count, and filter lent-out books
Persistence: round-trip through storage, survive refresh, drop malformed persisted rows, and recover from corrupt JSON / unavailable storage
